title: Mechanisms of Corneal Neuro-Immune Crosstalk
text:
We propose to investigate the role of the corneal parenchymal and resident immune cells in the
bidirectional crosstalk with the nerve system in neurotrophic keratitis. This project is focused on
discovery of the bioactive neurotrophic factors that are potentially synthesized by corneal cells
to maintain corneal integrity and neuronal homeostasis, and are capable of modulating
function and regenerative capacity of the corneal sensory nerves in neurotrophic keratitis.

title: Development of an Anti-Nerve Growth Factor Active Immunotherapy for Difficult-to-Manage Pain
text:
Chronic pain affects over 100 million Americans, but current treatment options like NSAIDs and opioids have
limited efficacy and several side effects. This research aims to develop a novel active immunotherapy targeting
nerve growth factor, a key mediator of chronic pain, to boost endogenous antibodies that block pain signaling. If
successful, this innovative immunotherapy could provide a safer and more effective option for managing chronic
pain that would improve the quality of life for millions of patients.

title: An integrated approach to understanding the molecular mechanisms of cation-coupled transport
text:
Ion-coupled transporters play important roles. We will characterize two Na+-coupled transporters that is
involved in health and serves as a prototype for the study of ion-coupled transport mechanisms
structurally and functionally. The expected outcome will improve our fundamental knowledge of active
transport and impact novel drug development.

title: Interparental Conflict and Parenting
text: External stressors have impact on family functioning that have increased rates of domestic violence and child maltreatment in the United States. Accordingly, developmental scientists, clinicians, and public policy advocates have underscored the public health significance of advancing an understanding of the impact on family functioning. The current application builds upon the aims of a multi-method, longitudinal study of families in a current R01 project by examining associations between interparental hostility and harsh parenting in families with young children, and how parental self-regulation may underlie these processes.

title: Optically Promoting Cardiac Maturation Using Engineered Peptides
text:
Stem cell-based regenerative therapies or in vitro investigations of cardiovascular disease
pathophysiology, drug screening, and toxicology studies heavily rely on stem cell quality. Here, peptide
nanostructures will be engineered to enable cells to be light responsive in a wireless and non-genetic manner,
which can ultimately be utilized as a strategy for converting optical cues to stimulatory signals that can improve
the structural and functional maturity of human stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. With this new approach, we
hope to alleviate the major technical barrier of CM immaturity, and therefore, better enable stem cell-based
cardiovascular research and related fields to flourish.

title: Investigating the heterogeneity and coordination of hematopoietic stem cells
text:
The proposed research can help improve the diagnosis and treatment of hematopoietic diseases,
particularly the blood and immune diseases associated with aging and TET2 mutations. It can also help
improve bone marrow transplantation and develop new blood regeneration treatments that are independent of
transplantation.

title: Comprehensive Characterization of LVV Integration and Impact on Host Cell Biology using Novel Genomic Technologies
text:
Lentiviral vectors (LVVs) are Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved for clinical use as gene delivery
systems and therapeutics; however, on November 28, 2023, it was announced that all clinically approved LVV-
transduced chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapies are under FDA investigation due to oncogenic
development resulting in hospitalization or death. Current methods used for characterizing LVV integration
remain limited and cannot resolve events in highly repetitive genomic regions or provide information regarding
transgene intactness, making it likely that integration events are not fully described. We aim to use a novel long-
read enrichment method, SMRTcap, to comprehensively characterize LVV integration profiles and transgene
integrity in experimental CAR T-cells, while also evaluating the impact of these events on host gene regulation
and splicing.

title: Postnatal and Prenatal Therapeutic Base Editing for Metabolic Diseases
text:
Phenylketonuria (PKU), the urea cycle disorders (UCDs), hereditary tyrosinemia type 1 (HT1), and mucopolysac-
charidosis type 1 (MPSI) are inherited disorders of metabolism that cause debilitating and even life-threatening
medical problems as early as birth. We seek to use a type of CRISPR gene editing technology, called base
editing, to directly and permanently correct gene mutations or otherwise alter genes at the DNA level in the liver,
either after or before birth—a “one-and-done” treatment strategy that could substantially improve the long-term
health of patients with these diseases.

title: Improving CAR-T efficacy against solid tumors by expanding lymph node reservoirs of “stem-like” CAR-T cells
text:
CAR-T cell therapy has induced dramatic responses in hematological malignancies, representing one of the
most remarkable therapeutic advances in the past decade, but efficacy in more common solid tumors has been
limited by rapid dysfunction and poor persistence of tumor-infiltrating CAR-T cells. Successful tumor responses
to immunotherapy are mediated by a subset of Tcf1+ T cells that resides in tumor-draining lymph nodes, where
they retain the capacity to self-renew, proliferate, and continually differentiate into short-lived effector cells to
sustain tumor killing. In this proposal, we will use a clinically relevant model of human lung cancer to investigate
whether CAR-T cell activity is limited by inefficient formation of a Tcf1+ reservoir and whether this defect can be
overcome using vaccination to expand lymph node reservoirs of Tcf1+ stem-like CAR-T cells, providing a strategy
to enhance CAR-T cell efficacy that can be readily translated to the clinic to improve patient outcomes.

title: Identifying the Determinants of Immunoediting During Glioblastoma Immunotherapy
text:
Cancer immunotherapies such as immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) have enabled improved clinical outcomes
across many solid tumors, but have yet to demonstrate efficacy in glioblastoma—the most common and aggressive
primary brain tumor. This proposal seeks to identify the tumor features that enable immune-mediated tumor
eradication in GBM patients receiving ICB, the mechanisms by which combining ICB with personalized cancer
vaccination promotes such features, and the remaining barriers to achieving durable tumor control. Elucidating
such mechanisms of immunotherapy response and resistance may guide future therapeutic strategies that achieve
improved clinical outcomes for GBM patients.

title: Circadian Regulation of Epithelial Immune Reponses in Asthma
text:
Circadian rhythms underlie numerous cellular functions in the lung, including how airway epithelia respond to
viral infections in health and in diseases such as asthma. The aim of the proposed work is to provide
mechanistic investigations of circadian regulation of epithelial immunity in human airway cells and how altered
responses contribute to asthma and asthma exacerbations. The long term goal will serve an important need in
providing biological knowledge of how to provide the optimal drug, in the optimal patient, at the optimal time of
day.

title: Combined IVUS/FFR microcatheter for guiding complex percutaneous coronary interventions
text:
Soon many of the minimally invasive procedures in the coronary arteries will be complex due to
anatomical factors as more patients already have stents and other implants in their hearts. While
anatomical imaging and blood flow (physiology) sensors are developed for this purpose and can
help clinicians to make better decisions with complementary information and procedure
optimization, sequential use of these devices increases risk, X-ray and contrast agent exposure,
procedure time and cost. This project aims to develop a microcatheter with both intravascular
imaging and physiology measurements to overcome this barrier for better guiding and
optimization of coronary interventions.

title: Label-free optical imaging for human mesoscale connectivity with a focus on deep brain stimulation targets
text:
This project will create a novel serial optical coherence scanner system that can image axonal tracts within
the brain at micrometer spatial resolution using unbiased label-free optical contrasts. This approach will
bridge macroscale, mesoscale, and microscale brain connectivity to create a platform that can be used for
future human connectome studies at the micron scale across the entire human brain.

title: Trophoblast development and placental susceptibility to cytomegalovirus infection
text:
Project Narrative.
Cytomegalovirus infection can disrupt placental function, causing intrauterine growth restriction and fetal
demise. Using a combination of trophoblast stem cell culture and a guinea pig model of congenital infection,
this project will investigate whether trophoblast differentiation and placental development sensitize the placenta
to infection-associated injury early and late in gestation.

title: Project 2: Ex Vivo Modeling and Analysis of Gastric Precancerous Lesions
text:
Project 2 will develop a renewable human gastric tissue culture model that represents stages of pre-neoplastic
progression. Investigators will be able to study and induce changes in gastric stem cells with the hopes of
understanding the mechanisms behind cancer development.

title: Mitigation of peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS) in MRI
text:
In the previous cycle we developed a detailed simulation of peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS) and proposed
methods to mitigate PNS in MRI, which is key to improve the image quality and acquisition speed of MRI
sequences commonly used in clinics. In this renewal application, we address remaining barriers to clinical and
industrial translation of our methods in order to achieve robust PNS mitigation for all patients and all MRI
examinations. To this aim, we extend our coil designs to reflect a diverse clinical population and examination
landmarks, and propose improved PNS monitoring tools that allow full utilization of the performance gains
brought by our designs.

title: Age related loss of immune resilience during response to severe respiratory viral infections
text:
Lay summary. Infections with respiratory viruses had unprecedented effects on human health leading to
increase use of critical care resources and mortality, especially among elders. In this project, we will use our
biorepository of lower airway and blood samples as well as data accessible to us to explore novel ways to
determine age-related molecular signatures that uncover novel pathways that lead to poor clinical outcomes.

title: Targeting Undruggable Transcription Factor HoxB13 to Inhibit Prostate Cancer Metastasis
text:
The proposed studies will provide a preclinical basis for the development of a nanoparticle capable of
delivering an effective and safe RNA-targeting gene therapy directly to castration-resistant prostate cancer
(CRPC) visceral and bone metastases for HoxB13 targeting. The successful translation of this system to future
medical applications could significantly enhance the well-being and reduce the mortality of men suffering from
metastatic CRPC, a condition that currently lacks a standard effective therapy. Additionally, the RNA-targeting
CRISPR/Cas13d system represents a highly flexible technology that could impact the larger field of
translational science, allowing for the design of Cas13d-based nanoparticles targeting other previously-
undruggable oncogenic transcription factors in prostate cancer and other solid tumors.

title: Biostatistics and Bioinformatics Core
text: The goal of the Biostatistics and Bioinformatics Core (BBC) is to collaborate with Phase 2 Center for Translational Viral Oncology (CTVO) investigators and other core scientists to enhance the quality of the research undertaken by the junior principal investigators and pilot project directors in the second phase of CTVO. The Core personnel have been selected because of their expertise in relevant areas of Biostatistics and Bioinformatics that are pertinent to CTVO projects and that foster teamwork in basic and translational research. The BBC will provide support in all stages of the study, beginning with the formulation of the research questions, experimental design, data collection, analysis, and interpretation, as well as writing of reports and dissemination of results. Core personnel have played a significant role in planning and data analyses for the proposed experimental plans in Phase 2 CTVO. The exact nature of the JPI/BBC collaboration will depend on the scientific emphasis and the project needs. In addition to direct support of the projects and other Cores, senior statisticians and bioinformaticians will also focus on the development of statistical methods and bioinformatics tools related to the needs of the projects in the CTVO. To achieve this goal, we will undertake the following Specific Aims: 1: Provide biostatistics and bioinformatics support on study design of clinical, laboratory and genomic studies and experiments for CTVO investigators; 2: Provide solutions and technology support services on data management and analyses to CTVO investigators, and 3: Develop novel biostatistics and bioinformatics methodology tools to address any issues that could not be addressed by existing methods. The ultimate goal is to provide custom-made and innovative biostatistics and bioinformatics support to successfully execute and complete the projects proposed in this Phase 2 CTVO grant renewal application.

title: Vascular-macrophage crosstalk in GBM immunosuppression
text: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a non-immunogenic “cold tumor”, refractory to immunotherapies. Failure of immunotherapies is largely attributed to the presence of immunosuppressive macrophages in the tumor microenvironment that hinder cytotoxic T-cell responses. Development of effective strategies to mitigate immunosuppression is therefore critical for improving immunotherapy outcomes for GBM. GBM-associated microglia and macrophages (GAMs) constitute about 50% of the tumor mass and are key drivers of immunosuppression and disease progression. However, the precise mechanisms by which GAMs acquire immunosuppressive and pro-tumorigenic phenotypes remain poorly defined. In prior work, we found that GBMassociated vascular cells (GVCs) produce immunomodulatory chemokines and cytokines that can potentially regulate the tumor-immune landscape. Our preliminary findings show that GAMs exposed to GVC-conditioned media upregulate immunosuppressive markers, and GVC-reprogrammed GAMs suppress cytotoxic T-cell proliferation, cytokine production, and effector activity while increasing the expression of exhaustion markers. Transcriptomic profiling identified SIGLEC10 as one of the most highly enriched genes in GVC-reprogrammed GAMs. Furthermore, analysis of patient single-cell datasets revealed enrichment of SIGLEC10Ά GAMs, particularly within the microglial fraction, with expression correlating with immunosuppressive markers and poor survival. In this study, we will test the hypothesis that GVCs reprogram GAMs towards an immunosuppressive state impeding cytotoxic T-cell responses and promote tumor growth. First, we aim to define the GVC-induced cellular states within GAMs using single-cell RNA-sequencing of ex vivo patient-derived cultures and in vivo GBM mouse models. Second, we will determine the role of SIGLEC10 in mediating GVC-induced immunosuppression using genetic and pharmacological approaches. Together, these studies will provide key insights into vascular–immune interactions that drive immunosuppression and identify SIGLEC10 as a potential novel GVC-induced checkpoint on GAMs that can be leveraged to enhance immunotherapy responses for GBM.
